top.title: AB de Villiers weighs in on Sandpapergate and claims Australia ball tampered in first test of 2018 series
top.description: Former South Africa captain AB de Villiers has ramped up the ongoing drama of sandpapergate, alleging Australia were ball tampering from the first Test of the 2018 series in Durban. The scandal initially centred around the third Test in Cape Town, where Cameron Bancroft was caught red-handed by television cameras using sandpaper to generate reverse swing. The drama reopened after more than eight years with the publication of Usman Khawaja ’s autobiography, which included a variety of new admissions, including that the same practice had been taking place in the second at Gqeberha, then known as Port Elizabeth. Bancroft and David Warner , who received lengthy bans for their roles alongside Steve Smith , corroborated Khawaja’s account. Meanwhile, a number of senior figures, including current Australia captain Pat Cummins and the former head coach Darren Lehmann , have issued fresh denials surrounding their own knowledge of the plot. Now De Villiers, who was a key part of the Proteas side in the ill-tempered series, has raised the stakes with new claims about the Durban game – Australia’s only win of the tour. Speaking on his own YouTube channel, ABD360, he said: “It’s become really personal for all the people involved and I do have sympathy for them. Obviously not sympathy for what took place on that day and who knows how many games before then. “I see everyone is sort of admitting that in Port Elizabeth it also happened. I can very much tell you Durban was no different, in the first Test. Go look at the footage. Absolutely no doubt in my mind. “It started in Durban, by the way, not in PE. I’m very happy for people to quote me on that. Australia captain Pat Cummins denied the allegations during a lengthy press conference in Sydney (Reuters) “We lost that first Test match in Durban with the ball reversing at a very, very interesting time. Way too early for anyone to reverse a ball at Kingsmead. Trust me, I’ve played a lot of cricket there. “So whatever they did there, whether it was sandpaper or (a) nail, I don’t care. The fact of the matter is they were caught and everyone knew. Just stand up as say ‘we were wrong’. A lot is at stake now because they lied.” Cummins has repeatedly distanced himself from the tampering allegations, rejecting any role in the events during a long press conference in Sydney. He has since received the unanimous backing of the Cricket Australia board to continue as captain following growing speculation over his future. Khawaja and Warner, on the other hand, have been stood down from commentary duties on Fox Cricket for the ongoing England T20 series. “I just feel they should have stuck together as a unit. They threw the guys under the bus and forced a situation like this to pop up again eight years later,” concluded De Villiers.

top.description: Stanford women's basketball head coach Kate Paye reacts during the first half of the Cardinal's loss against the Washington Huskies on Friday at Alaska Airlines Arena in Seattle. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images) The Stanford women's basketball team is off to its worst start since 2017 after falling to host Portland 73-62 on Sunday night. Point guard Hailee Swain, who entered averaging 20.5 points per game, was held to 10 on 4-for-14 shooting (0-for-5 from 3-point). Inés Sotelo Míguez scored a team-high 18 Sara Mangan led Portland with 18 points off the bench. The last time these teams met, Stanford squandered a 13-point second-half lead to end its 2024-25 season in a 69-68 overtime defeat in the first round of the WBIT. The 2017-18 Cardinal suffered losses to No. 5 Ohio State, No. 1 Connecticut and again against the Buckeyes (then ranked ninth) in their first seven games, only to finish second in the Pac-12 and advance to the Sweet Sixteen. These 2026-27 Cardinal suffered losses to unranked Arizona and Portland sandwiched around a program-worst 55-point defeat to No. 16 Washington. top.title: ‘Monies Borrowed Are Being Used For Investments, Infrastructure’, Umahi Inspects Coastal Road Bridges

Umahi revealed this as he inspected the Coastal Road Bridges on Sunday. According to him, the road projects are not the only investments President Tinubu is spending the borrowed monies on, as the Federal Government also has the vision of investing in housing for rentals. Umahi while inspecting the coastal road bridges on Sunday, November 22, 2026. “As far back as six months, section one was already fully completed. Section two, which is about 53 kilometers, is also already completed. It has road architecture such as solar lights, underground drainage, and the walkway. “So, it’s something that is out of this world in terms of performance, where you have over 200 kilometres plus being done within two and a half years. It’s a performance that no other contractor in Africa has been able to achieve. “I have bragging rights as the Minister of Works over these projects because I am very proud of them. I have bragging rights for the President because when you are on this coastal way, it is quite relieving. “Imagine if we can go all the way from Lagos to Calabar on this kind of road. All these roads are investments of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. And when you ask about the monies which are being borrowed. They are being used for infrastructure. They are being used for investment in infrastructure. “And investors are asking how they can return the investments on this road. But we are still considering their request because we want to install CCTV, we want to rent houses. We want to buy land where we can have a lot of facilities for tourism, factories, and others. “And these projects are profit-driven for the Federal Republic of Nigeria. One of the completed coastal road bridges inspected on Sunday, November 22, 2026. Tinubu said the proposed borrowing would help finance part of the Federal Government’s budget deficit and fund projects across critical sectors, including defence, transportation, agriculture, power, education and health. top.title: Raiders’ Klint Kubiak shrugs off Denver return following Broncos loss
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Raiders’ Klint Kubiak shrugs off Denver return following Broncos loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Going home feels great until you leave with a 38-24 loss. Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak had zero interest in reminiscing after his Denver Broncos homecoming ended in defeat on Nov. 22. Kubiak grew up in the Denver area, spent four seasons across two stints on the Broncos’ coaching staff and watched his father, Gary Kubiak, win a Super Bowl as Denver’s head coach. Still, when reporters asked about returning to Empower Field at Mile High, Kubiak shut down the nostalgia immediately. “Yeah, I could. I don’t want to,” Kubiak said. “I wanted to win this game today. And we didn’t win. So we gotta go win next week.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Las Vegas fell to 4-7 after digging an early 17-0 hole. Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza sparked a comeback before halftime, hitting running back Ashton Jeanty for a 68-yard touchdown in the second quarter before finding tight end Ian Thomas for a 19-yard score in the third to tie the game at 17. Mendoza finished 18-of-37 for 267 yards, three touchdowns and an interception while playing without injured star tight end Brock Bowers. Jeanty carried the offense with 79 rushing yards on 11 attempts and 90 receiving yards on five catches. Denver’s pass rush also sacked Mendoza five times, and nine Las Vegas penalties for 63 yards stalled momentum. Denver improved to 8-2 behind rookie running back Jonah Coleman, who pounded out 111 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries. Quarterback Bo Nix added 225 passing yards and a score. Wide receiver Jack Bech caught a 7-yard touchdown pass from Mendoza with 4:29 left to pull the Raiders within 31-24, but cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian sealed the win with a 35-yard pick-six just after coming out of the two-minute warning. Kubiak expressed optimism that Bowers can return from ankle and quadriceps injuries when Las Vegas visits the Cleveland Browns next Sunday night. Kubiak gets another shot at the Broncos on Dec. 20 in Las Vegas. Until then, sentimental storylines remain off limits. top.description: FBL-ITA-SERIEA-ATALANTA-INTER MILAN - AFP Inter head coach Cristian Chivu has delivered a stinging assessment of his side's mental fragility after they squandered multiple leads in a breathtaking 4-4 draw against Atalanta. The Nerazzurri boss claimed his players "failed the exam" during a chaotic evening in Bergamo that saw them surrender a two-goal cushion on three separate occasions. Late collapse ruins Pio Esposito's hat-trick Atalanta snatched a dramatic point in Bergamo through Charles De Ketelaere’s second goal and a stoppage-time penalty from Franck, cancelling out Petar Sucic’s spot-kick that had made it 4-2. That late collapse ruined a landmark evening for Pio Esposito , who followed up his strong Nations League displays for Italy by netting his first Serie A hat-trick. Inter’s frustration was compounded by two penalty calls. The visitors felt Davide Zappacosta deserved a red card rather than a booking for a goal-line elbow clearance, before Alessandro Bastoni conceded the decisive late spot-kick for an unintentional handball with his arms raised above his shoulder. Chivu slams 'soft and shallow' Nerazzurri display Speaking to DAZN Italia , Chivu lambasted his side's lack of edge. "We were leading 2-0, 3-1 and 4-2, so this is the regret," Chivu said after the game. "We had an idea of what we should’ve done and did not do, we should’ve controlled the advantage, then when we felt them snapping at our heels, we immediately restored the two-goal cushion. "I think we failed the exam in the final minutes. It’s hard to say why we were unable to control the lead. We have to congratulate Atalanta, as they sensed that we were a bit shallow, and pumped crosses into the box, put bodies in there, while we were a little soft compared to our usual approach. "I’m sorry, I see this as two gifted points, but we will learn from it and know now to let the intensity and mentality drop in the next games." He also pinpointed lapses at set-pieces and inside the box. "The second Atalanta goal came from a corner, identical to one where Pepo had just made a great save moments earlier, so we did not learn from it," Chivu continued. "When we got to 4-2, our defence was then static in a chaotic situation. We need a certain determination and focus in these situations, and we were negligent in that area today." Chivu altered his wide setup late on, though he insisted mentality mattered most. "I felt we were suffering on the wings, partly because we were too soft, we were allowing the space to put the crosses in too easily. I decided to put Marcus Thuram wide to help out Djed Spence in the final stages," Chivu added. "It’s a matter of desire to go into the duels, to be more determined, not just put bodies behind the ball, because if you don’t have the right intensity then a single error can be costly." top.description: Inigo Perez explains why reveals why Villarreal struggled to stop Barcelona’s comeback: ‘Perhaps it was a case of pressing’ Villarreal manager Inigo Perez admitted that his team struggled to cope with Barcelona’s sustained attacking pressure after surrendering a two-goal advantage in their 3-2 La Liga defeat at Spotify Camp Nou . The Yellow Submarine had enjoyed an impressive opening 35 minutes, where they scored twice, but Barcelona’s second-half response left them without a point. Speaking after the match, Perez defended his players while acknowledging that Villarreal needed to manage possession more effectively once Hansi Flick’s side began taking control. Perez reflects on Villarreal’s missed opportunity vs Barcelona Perez was particularly disappointed that Villarreal could not turn their excellent opening performance into a positive result. He recognised that Barcelona’s attacking quality made protecting a two-goal advantage difficult, particularly when the hosts continued applying pressure after taking the lead. “When you find yourself 0–2 down after 35 very good minutes, you know they’re going to come at you relentlessly; even after they’d scored their third, they carried on in the same vein. “Something was missing. I wouldn’t want to say anything that I can’t back up with the video later. It hurts to have played 35 such good minutes and come away with nothing.” Villarreal manager explains his tactical approach The Villarreal manager also explained that his team had prepared specifically to challenge Barcelona higher up the pitch and did not intend to defend deep. Inigo Perez has analysed the 3-2 defeat to Barcelona. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) He explained that pressing Barcelona and exploiting the spaces behind their defensive structure had been central to Villarreal’s preparation. “Before the match, we talked about pressing high up the pitch. We’d practised the build-up to the first goal and also running into the spaces. “We knew it would be a back-and-forth affair. And we knew that a two-goal lead wouldn’t be enough. We needed to hold on a bit longer.” He also noted why retreating into a defensive shape was unlikely to provide a solution against Flick’s team. “Against that kind of pressing, where they combine physicality with a high level of quality, you have to defend very well and keep attacking them. It’s difficult. “That must be the approach against Barça. Just sitting back or defending won’t work.” Perez refuses to blame his players for Barcelona comeback The Villarreal coach referenced his team’s previous experience against Liverpool when discussing the difficulty of responding to sustained pressure. The Red Wings have watched Larkin blossom into a star for them over the course of his 11 years in the NHL. Faces come and go, but iconic play-by-play voice Ken Daniels has seen his entire career to this point. Eventually, Shawn Horcoff was named interim general manager. Horcoff maintained that a Larkin trade needed to make sense for Detroit. The former Detroit captain played 10 games for the Red Wings this year before refusing to play on October 29. Horcoff waited quite a while, and a deal finally came together on Sunday night. How these teams will look following the trade certainly remains to be seen. top.description: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso reacts in the dugout during the Premier League match at Stamford Bridge, London. Picture date: Saturday November 21, 2026. (Photo by John Walton/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images Another aggravating weekend in the Land of the Blues, with another historic home defeat suffered against one of our historic rivals. First, it were Spurs winning at the Bridge for just the second time since 1990. Now, it’s Leeds United walking away with all three points for the first time since 1999. And they probably were partying like it, too. And it’s not like either of those two results were undeserved. There were no miracles here. We weren’t undone by an unlucky bounce or an egregious call, even if the penalty called on Morgan Rogers was a bit harsh (if the shoulder or shirt sleeve count for offside, it shouldn’t be a handball). Spurs and Leeds, both, were by far the superior team — in motivation, in intensity, in cohesion, in teamwork, in execution … in all aspects. This weekend’s 4-1 (four!) embarrassment against the latter was likened in commentary to a training exercise against a youth team for the visitors. While Clearlake may wish the team to be that young for future profit considerations, in theory, we are a senior professional outfit with actual aspirations and ambitions of winning and trophies. The only way those objectives could be any further away from us at the moment is if we had actually been dissolved by the UK government back in 2022. At least that’s what it feels like, even 36 hours removed from the result. And Xabi Alonso wasn’t exactly trying to put a positive spin on things either with his post-match comments. “After the equaliser […] we lost completely the momentum. Until then we were doing okay, I think that we were creating, playing a lot on the pitch, we were coming out for the pressure, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing and after that we never got the good feeling mentally in any moment. “[We] are in a fragile moment mentally, confidence when we receive a punch that we didn’t recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling. [We] still have many minutes to play and it’s not that the game is over [but] we didn’t recover that good momentum.” As Mike Tyson once famously said, everyone has a plan ‘til they get punched in the mouth. Except when we get punched in the mouth, we forget not only the plan (however good or bad that might have been) but we seem to completely forget how to even play football. Unfortunately, this isn’t a new issue either. We’ve struggled with these sorts of situations ever since the galaxy brains in charge dismantled the team and put up a kindergarten in its stead. top.title: 'You don't win 345 matches just by defending' - Diego Simeone hits back at critics after breaking Luis Aragones' all-time La Liga record
top.description: FBL-ESP-LIGA-ATLETICO-BARCELONA - AFP Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone has hit back at critics who label his side overly defensive after breaking Luis Aragones' all-time La Liga wins record on Sunday. The Argentine secured his 345th Spanish top-flight victory with a comfortable 3-0 triumph at Getafe, moving past the late club legend's long-standing benchmark of 344 wins. Argentine coach surpasses club legend Simeone claimed his 345th La Liga victory in just his 567th match , needing 189 fewer games than Aragones took to reach 344 before his final win in 2004. Goals from Alex Baena and Johnny Cardoso put Atletico in control by half-time, both assisted by Julian Alvarez . Alejandro Grimaldo added a late penalty after Djene Dakonam was sent off following a VAR review for fouling Alexander Sorloth. Simeone rejects defensive football label Reflecting on the milestone after the match, Simeone admitted the achievement meant a great deal: "It makes me happy. I don't usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this." Despite evolving Atletico's style considerably since arriving in 2011, the coach still faces familiar jibes about his tactics. Addressing the scrutiny on Spanish television channel Movistar , he added: "Then there's the constant criticism we face. I don't place much value on it, but I do take note of it. "This narrative that we're a defensive team, as if we're always playing solely to defend. You don't win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?" Longevity defines remarkable Atletico reign Taking over a struggling club almost 15 years ago, Simeone has transformed Atletico into Spanish football's established third force, disrupting Real Madrid and Barcelona while lifting eight trophies. Although rival coaches may hold higher win percentages or larger trophy hauls, few can match his resilience and consistency at the top level. Even the deepest scars of his tenure, two Champions League final defeats to Real, one on penalties and another in extra time after a stoppage-time equaliser, failed to derail him. Instead, the black-clad tactician has maintained the same touchline intensity, passing the all-time record from one Atletico great to another 22 years after Aragones set it. Atletico chase La Liga title leaders Sunday's result made it eight wins in nine league games, lifting Atletico to 31 points , just two behind Real and five adrift of leaders Barcelona. With Baena, Alvarez and Cardoso clicking, Simeone's side have built real momentum heading into the winter schedule. Sustaining this attacking sharpness will be vital if they are to turn another strong run into a genuine title charge.

top.title: ‘Listen to me’: What John Harbaugh ran up to Liam Coen and said after Giants beat Jaguars
top.description: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images The New York Giants picked up a statement 23-18 win against the Jacksonville Jaguars at MetLife Stadium. Both teams came into the game with a lot of confidence, but not many people would’ve put their money on the Giants getting the job done. That’s how good the Jaguars have been this season, which is probably why their coach, Liam Coen, earned some praise from John Harbaugh after the game. John Harbaugh praises Liam Coen after Giants beat Jaguars The game between the New York Giants and the Jacksonville Jaguars was a great watch. Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson’s unit intercepted MVP candidate Trevor Lawrence twice and generated constant pressure. That led to Jacksonville converting just one of six red-zone trips and settling for two field goals early, four overall. There was some controversy in the end, with a refereeing decision going against the Jaguars, but their head coach Coen still gracefully shook Harbaugh’s hand. Cameras saw that exchange, where Harbaugh was seen running up to Coen, shaking his hand, pulling him closer and offering him and his side some big praise. The Athletic’s Ian O’Connor transcribed the Giants coach’s words on X : “Hey, listen to me. You got a hell of a team. And you have done a great job with this football team. You are a very well-coached football team.” Harbaugh is one of the best coaches in the NFL, and he has seen it all in the game over the last few decades. He knows what it takes to build a championship-winning side. That is why the 64-year-old’s praise for Coen should mean so much to the Jaguars coach, who is still very young in his coaching career. Despite the defeat, Jacksonville are still 7-3 for the season and remain on top of the AFC South standings. It remains to be seen how they will bounce back when they face the Titans next week. top.description: Jashaun Corbin #36 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty Backup running back has been something of a Bermuda triangle for the Dallas Cowboys this year, going back to training camp when the two main contenders for the RB2 job were 2025 draftees Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah. After three months of OTAs, training camp and preseason games, neither earned the spot and were waived. The Cowboys went with veteran backup Malik Davis, but he suffered a season-ending hip injury days before the opener. Emari Demercado came and went, and Tyler Goodson stabilized the job before he, too, got hurt. Now it is Jashaun Corbin, signed from the practice squad, getting his shot–and maybe making things difficult when Goodson does return. Corbin is the quintessential NFL journeyman, having bounced through two stints with the Giants, as well as spots with the Panthers, Patriots and Falcons. He spent training camp with the Cowboys this summer, and has also dipped into the UFL, leading the league in rushing in 2024 with San Antonio and leading the league in rushing attempts with Orlando this year. Now, Corbin is with the Cowboys. Jashaun Corbin May ‘Get More Playing Time’ And his Cowboys debut was notable. Corbin had five carries for 32 yards, his first NFL carries since 2023 with the Giants. He also was credited for a very good blitz pickup. Cowboys team site writer Tommy Yarrish wrote of Corbin, “Cowboys RB Jashaun Corbin got his shot at RB2 this afternoon, and pass protection reps like this to set up big plays could really help his case to get more playing time.” Joe Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News wrote: “This pass pro was so good, that I assumed it was Javonte Williams. (FRANCK FIFE) Nigerian Taiwo Awoniyi scored for Coventry City and later had to be substituted after collapsing in a Premier League victory over Crystal Palace at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND TAIWO AWONIYI (Coventry City) The striker scored his third goal for Coventry in a 3-2 win against bottom club Palace, but his afternoon came to a bizarre premature end. Awoniyi netted in the fifth minute with a close-range finish into the far corner from Jack Rudoni's pass to put Coventry 1-0 up at the CBS Arena. But the 29-year-old, signed from Nottingham Forest in the close season, was forced to miss the last 45 minutes after going down clutching his leg in pain while the players were lining up to start the second half. Awoniyi had to be helped up off the ground by two Palace players and limped off, forcing bemused Coventry boss Frank Lampard to make an unexpected substitution. Lampard admitted afterwards that Awoniyi felt a slight problem with his ankle from the first half. SPAIN YASSIR ZABIRI (Racing Santander) Moroccan forward Zabiri struck twice in the opening stages to help Santander beat Real Sociedad 3-2 in La Liga. (INA FASSBENDER) Borussia Dortmund coach Niko Kovac backed struggling winger Ethan Nwaneri to find form ahead of Tuesday's Champions League clash at parent club Arsenal. Nwaneri, 19, joined Dortmund on a season-long loan from the Gunners on deadline day, but has not been a beneficiary of the German club's impressive start to the campaign. Unbeaten in Germany this season, Dortmund sit two points clear of defending champions Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga table. But Nwaneri has just one assist in 13 appearances and has gone from being a regular starter to occupying largely a bench role, with some media outlets reporting the loan spell could end early in January. Nwaneri burst onto the scene with Arsenal, becoming the youngest player in Premier League history when he made his debut aged 15 years and 181 days in September 2022. The teenager scored 10 goals and laid on two assists in 51 matches for the Gunners, but moved to French side Marseille last season chasing more game time. After scoring in his opening match, a 3-1 win over Lens in January, Nwaneri only netted once more during his time at the Ligue 1 club and was mostly relegated to the bench. Clearly a fan of a fast start, Nwaneri assisted a goal in his opening Dortmund match but has yet to register another goal or assist. During the recent international break, Nwaneri laid on two goals as England U21s beat France U21s 3-2. - 'Fierce competition' - Speaking on Thursday, Kovac praised Nwaneri's performance for England and backed the teenager for a bright future, at Dortmund and beyond. nigeria.title: Abuja entrepreneurs struggle with soaring costs, shrinking demand
nigeria.description: Abuja entrepreneurs struggle daily as rising costs, shrinking purchasing power and inconsistent income threaten the survival of enterprises they have spent years building. From bakers battling unreliable electricity and rising ingredient prices to fabric sellers struggling with customers who buy on credit and fashion designers waiting for payments, entrepreneurs across different sectors say the harsh economic climate is making it increasingly difficult to sustain their businesses. They say their income is often insufficient to cover the cost of running their businesses, leaving them with little profit and, in some cases, mounting debts. Aisha Dikko, a baker and food vendor, said her journey into business had been marked by sacrifices, unexpected challenges and lessons she never anticipated when she started. Inspired by her mother, who was also a baker, Dikko said what began as a passion gradually developed into a business. However, she admitted that she had initially underestimated the demands of running an enterprise. “I thought it would be relatively easy. People loved my cakes and small chops whenever I made them at home, so I assumed turning that into a business would be straightforward,” she said. She said she soon realised that running a business required much more than the ability to bake, as she had to learn about pricing, marketing, customer relations, production and financial management. Although she has recorded some growth over the years, Dikko said fluctuating prices of ingredients and supplies remained a major challenge, with the cost of restocking often changing from one purchase to another. Beyond rising costs, she said the declining purchasing power of customers had also affected her business, with some making unrealistic offers for products whose production costs were considerably higher. Dikko recalled an instance when a prospective customer offered N70,000 for desserts for 300 guests, even though her estimated cost of providing desserts for just 100 guests was about N300,000. She further explained that electricity had been one of her most difficult operational challenges. The situation, she added, became so frustrating that she considered abandoning the business. The installation of solar power by her husband, however, provided some relief and enabled her to continue operating from home, although she still relies on gas and an inverter for some operations. She called on the government to provide more practical support for small businesses, arguing that access to loans alone would not address the challenges entrepreneurs face. For fabric seller Aisha Kabir, the challenge of keeping a business afloat is largely tied to cash flow, particularly as more customers struggle to pay for goods purchased on credit. Kabir, who has been in the fabric business for over a decade, said sales on credit had made it increasingly difficult to maintain consistent cash flow. nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Army has commended Air Peace and its Chairman, Dr Allen Onyema, for introducing a discounted one-way domestic air fare of ₦80,000 for serving and retired personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces. The committee also urged other airlines and corporate organisations in the country to emulate the gesture as part of efforts to improve the welfare of military personnel and veterans. The commendation was contained in a statement issued on Sunday by the Chairman of the committee, Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua, representing Katsina Central Senatorial District. According to the statement, the initiative was unveiled on November 16, 2026, during the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference in Abuja. The committee said the discounted fare was available to eligible military personnel who had served in the Nigerian Armed Forces since 1960, across all domestic routes. It added that Air Peace would also bear the cost of tickets for regional and international flights, with beneficiaries required to pay only applicable taxes and charges. Describing the initiative as a patriotic gesture, the committee said it was a practical demonstration of appreciation for the sacrifices made by serving and retired military personnel in defending the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. It noted that members of the Armed Forces had continued to make enormous sacrifices, often at great personal cost, and deserved tangible support that would improve their welfare and that of their families. “By reducing the burden of air travel, Air Peace has demonstrated that patriotism is not only spoken in times of ceremony, but shown in practical action that touches the lives of those who serve,” the statement said. The committee particularly praised Onyema for what it described as his consistent commitment to humanitarian causes, national development and support for the Nigerian military. It also endorsed the airline chairman’s call for the military leadership to establish a robust verification system to ensure that only genuine beneficiaries access the concession. According to the committee, such a mechanism would help make the initiative sustainable, transparent and free from abuse. It appealed to other airlines and corporate organisations to support the Armed Forces, describing the welfare of serving personnel and veterans as a collective national responsibility. “The private sector has a critical role to play in complementing the efforts of the Federal Government in improving the welfare and morale of our troops and veterans,” it said. nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor The Federal Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Valmont Industries Inc., the world’s largest manufacturer of pivot irrigation systems, to accelerate the implementation of its flagship Irrigate Nigeria Programme. The agreement also provides for the establishment of an irrigation equipment production plant in Nigeria in partnership with the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI), as part of efforts to boost local manufacturing and reduce dependence on imported irrigation technology. The Presidential Implementation Committee on Technology Transfer (PICTT) signed the agreement with Valmont at the weekend. In a statement issued by NASENI on Sunday, the Chairman of PICTT, Dr Dahiru Muhammed, who is also coordinating the implementation of the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, said the agreement formally brought Valmont, through its Valley Irrigation brand, on board as a major partner in developing irrigation infrastructure across the country. Muhammed, who signed the agreement alongside Valmont’s Regional Vice President for the Middle East and Africa, Mr Kalle Autto, described the partnership as a significant step towards expanding mechanised irrigation in Nigeria. He said: “This MoU officially brings the biggest pivot irrigation manufacturer in the world on board as a major partner in building irrigation infrastructure across Nigeria under the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, the flagship irrigation programme of this administration.” He explained that beyond developing irrigation infrastructure, Valmont had agreed to work with NASENI to establish a local production facility for irrigation equipment. “Just as importantly, this partnership comes with the transfer of know-how and capacity building for Nigerians, which is precisely what technology transfer is all about,” he added. The agreement also provides for a pilot irrigation programme covering 40,000 hectares in Adamawa State. The project will be implemented in collaboration with the Nigeria Incentive-Based Risk Sharing System for Agricultural Lending (NIRSAL) and the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF). While PICTT will lead the overall implementation of the programme, NASENI will drive the adoption and domestication of the technology. The partnership is also expected to create opportunities for collaboration with the University of Nebraska and the Robert B. Muhammed said key stakeholders had already expressed interest in expanding irrigation infrastructure through the partnership, describing the development as a vote of confidence in the programme. nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army under Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued 18 children abducted by suspected terrorists in Kaduna State, while intensifying efforts to secure the release of four others still held by the fleeing kidnappers. The children, members of the Boys’ and Girls’ Brigade, were reportedly abducted early Sunday, November 22, 2026, while participating in a morning group road walk at Mother-Cat Community in the Kachia/Kajuru general area of the state. Confirming the rescue in a statement on Sunday night, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said troops of the 1 Division Nigerian Army, operating under Sector 1 of Operation Fansan Yamma, launched a rescue operation shortly after receiving a distress call. Anele said troops of Sub-Sector 5 immediately mobilised and pursued the abductors through surrounding bushes, advancing towards Rehina Riverside, where some of the children were found abandoned by the fleeing criminals. She said the troops sustained the pursuit along the river line, rescuing additional victims and bringing the number of recovered children to 18. According to the Army, sustained military pressure forced the abductors to abandon the children as they fled deeper into the surrounding forest. The statement added that troops had extended their search operations along the Ankwa–Kabode–Pachi link road and towards the Awon and Akwondo general areas to locate the remaining four children and apprehend those responsible for the abduction. The Army assured the families of the victims and the general public of its commitment to rescuing all the abducted children. It also said troops would sustain offensive operations and intelligence-led patrols to protect vulnerable communities and prevent further attacks. nigeria.title: How Oyibo, BEDC worker was murdered 4 months into marriage
nigeria.description: •Disco, Delta community mourn •Family shattered, seeks justice By Egufe Yafugborhi & Cynthia Alo Oscar Eze, popularly known as Oyibo or NEPA Man, left home on Monday, November 16, 2026, for another routine assignment as an operations personnel of the Benin Electricity Distribution Company, BEDC, Agbor Business Unit. The 38-year-old had no reason to suspect that the day’s work in Umunede, Ika North-East Local Government Area of Delta State, would be his last. Four months after remarrying following the death of his first wife, Eze was brutally murdered in circumstances that have left his pregnant wife, young son and elderly mother devastated, while colleagues and residents mourn a man widely remembered for his cheerful disposition. His last assignment took him to a relatively isolated suburb of Idumu-Oba, with sparsely distributed buildings. While working alongside other workmen at a property apparently undergoing finishing, he was ambushed by a gang of youths. A CCTV camera at the premises captured the horrifying encounter. The assailants accosted him around the small entrance gate, dragged him into the compound and repeatedly stabbed him with daggers as other workmen watched in fear. He sustained multiple injuries to his upper body and died shortly afterwards. He was rushed to hospital, where he was confirmed dead. The police subsequently confirmed that Eze was attacked on November 16, at about 1.15 p.m., during a power disconnection exercise at Ileje Quarters, Umunede. According to BEDC management, the property he had disconnected owed the company almost N300,000 in electricity bills. His attackers allegedly trailed him after the disconnection. A legitimate assignment to earn a living ended in a gruesome killing, leaving a community asking how a familiar electricity worker could have become the target of such violence. A young marriage shattered Beyond the circumstances of his death lies the tragedy of a family whose hopes have been abruptly shattered. Eze’s first wife died about two years ago, leaving him with a son. He subsequently remarried barely four months before his death. His new wife was reportedly pregnant. A neighbour close to the BEDC office affirmed: “His first wife, who had a child for him, died about two years ago. Then he remarried four months ago. “I don’t know where the new wife is from. His former wife was from here (Umunede). Oyibo lived at Idumu-Oba.” At the compound where Eze lived, a neighbour said his wife was taken away on the day news of the killing reached them. “We don’t know anything about it. nigeria.title: Ajaokuta: NES blames collapse of long-term planning for 40-year stalemate
nigeria.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The President, Nigerian Economic Society (NES), Dr. Baba Musa, has blamed the collapse of long-term economic planning for the failure of the Ajaokuta Steel Company to become operational more than four decades after its establishment. Musa, who spoke at the National Growth & Development Forum (NGDF) 2026 in Abuja, said Nigeria lost the link between economic planning and execution, resulting in the abandonment or underperformance of strategic national projects. “History demands candour. Somewhere along the way, we lost vital links between plan and performance. We built, but did not always maintain,” he said. According to him, the oil windfall of the 1970s diverted the country from agriculture and non-oil exports which had previously sustained the economy. “The oil windfall of the 1970s drew us away from the agriculture and non-oil exports that had sustained us. Strategic projects such as the Ajaokuta Steel Complex, begun with great promise, have yet to fulfil it four decades on. “And when formal planning gave way in the mid-1980s, long-term strategy too often yielded to visions that changed with administrations,” Musa said. He said Nigeria must learn from its past policy failures to avoid repeating mistakes that have undermined economic development. “The Nigeria we want must be built upon the Nigeria we have, and the Nigeria we have,” he added. The NES president also expressed concern that economic reforms had yet to translate into shared prosperity, noting that about 63 per cent of Nigerians, estimated at 140 million people, lived below the poverty line in 2025, according to the World Bank. “Macroeconomic stability is necessary, but it is not yet shared prosperity. A stable exchange rate is not yet a full dinner table. Stability is the foundation; it is not the building,” he said. Musa called for an economy that generates jobs, supports the poor, boosts domestic production, invests in human capital and promotes disciplined public finance and credible institutions. Similarly, President, Capital Market Academics of Nigeria, Prof. Uche Uwaleke, said economic reforms must be measured by their impact on citizens’ welfare, job creation, purchasing power and poverty reduction. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. It requires the confidence to own one’s value, the clarity to communicate one’s contributions and the intentionality to build visibility that translates into meaningful influence. These conversations defined The Executive Woman Summit (TEWS) 2.0 , which brought together hundreds of executive women, corporate professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging leaders at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Convened by Bola Matel-Okoh , a dual-qualified attorney (called to both the New York and Nigerian Bars), Executive Coach, Non-Executive Director at Wema Bank, and CEO of BMO Advisory Services , the second edition of the summit was themed Playing to Win: Elevate Your Vision, Value and Visibility. It provided an intentional platform for candid conversations, practical insights and strategic alliances on what it takes for women to advance, lead and thrive in today’s evolving corporate landscape. In her opening address, Matel-Okoh challenged women to rethink how they approach professional visibility, authority and advancement. According to her, competence is merely the baseline; it is not enough if you are unwilling to communicate your value, own your voice and position yourself for higher-stakes opportunities. This philosophy also came through in her cover interview with THISDAY Glitterati ahead of the summit, where she offered a compelling perspective on the distinction between holding a powerful position and exercising genuine influence. “A powerful position gives you formal authority. Influence determines how deeply your leadership shapes people’s thinking, decisions and actions. A title may secure your place in a meeting, but credibility makes people listen,” she explained. She also challenged the assumption that excellent work will automatically speak for itself, encouraging women to communicate their contributions with evidence and confidence. “What problem did you solve? What result did you produce? What changed because of your leadership?” she asked, highlighting the importance of making professional value visible to the decision-makers who influence career progression and boardroom opportunities. “There is no need to diminish your achievements to make others comfortable. You can be gracious and still be clear about the value you bring,” she added. The summit featured a distinguished line-up of women shaping leadership, business, finance, entertainment and corporate governance. entertainment.description: The Metropolitan Club, Lagos, was transformed into a gathering of some of the most influential names in Nigeria’s energy industry as the Women in Energy Network (WIEN) hosted its 2026 Gala & Awards. Beyond the glamour, elegant conversations and celebrations, the event carried a clear message: it is time to move beyond conversations about inclusion and focus on measurable progress. In her address, WIEN President Eyono Fatayi-Williams emphasised that progress must be visible, measurable and sustained. “As we celebrate six years, we also have to ask ourselves an important question: What do the next six years look like? entertainment.title: Tochukwu Ekoh: What My Friend’s Passing Taught Me About Kindness
entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? What was the reason for that reconnection, and why did it have to end this way? The timing of certain events leaves you with more questions than answers. sports.title: AB de Villiers weighs in on Sandpapergate and claims Australia ball tampered in first test of 2018 series
sports.description: Former South Africa captain AB de Villiers has ramped up the ongoing drama of sandpapergate, alleging Australia were ball tampering from the first Test of the 2018 series in Durban. The scandal initially centred around the third Test in Cape Town, where Cameron Bancroft was caught red-handed by television cameras using sandpaper to generate reverse swing. The drama reopened after more than eight years with the publication of Usman Khawaja ’s autobiography, which included a variety of new admissions, including that the same practice had been taking place in the second at Gqeberha, then known as Port Elizabeth. Bancroft and David Warner , who received lengthy bans for their roles alongside Steve Smith , corroborated Khawaja’s account. Meanwhile, a number of senior figures, including current Australia captain Pat Cummins and the former head coach Darren Lehmann , have issued fresh denials surrounding their own knowledge of the plot. Now De Villiers, who was a key part of the Proteas side in the ill-tempered series, has raised the stakes with new claims about the Durban game – Australia’s only win of the tour. Speaking on his own YouTube channel, ABD360, he said: “It’s become really personal for all the people involved and I do have sympathy for them. Obviously not sympathy for what took place on that day and who knows how many games before then. “I see everyone is sort of admitting that in Port Elizabeth it also happened. I can very much tell you Durban was no different, in the first Test. Go look at the footage. Absolutely no doubt in my mind. “It started in Durban, by the way, not in PE. I’m very happy for people to quote me on that. Australia captain Pat Cummins denied the allegations during a lengthy press conference in Sydney (Reuters) “We lost that first Test match in Durban with the ball reversing at a very, very interesting time. Way too early for anyone to reverse a ball at Kingsmead. Trust me, I’ve played a lot of cricket there. “So whatever they did there, whether it was sandpaper or (a) nail, I don’t care. The fact of the matter is they were caught and everyone knew. Just stand up as say ‘we were wrong’. A lot is at stake now because they lied.” Cummins has repeatedly distanced himself from the tampering allegations, rejecting any role in the events during a long press conference in Sydney. He has since received the unanimous backing of the Cricket Australia board to continue as captain following growing speculation over his future. Khawaja and Warner, on the other hand, have been stood down from commentary duties on Fox Cricket for the ongoing England T20 series. “I just feel they should have stuck together as a unit. They threw the guys under the bus and forced a situation like this to pop up again eight years later,” concluded De Villiers.

sports.description: FBL-ITA-SERIEA-ATALANTA-INTER MILAN - AFP Inter head coach Cristian Chivu has delivered a stinging assessment of his side's mental fragility after they squandered multiple leads in a breathtaking 4-4 draw against Atalanta. Inter’s frustration was compounded by two penalty calls. Chivu slams 'soft and shallow' Nerazzurri display Speaking to DAZN Italia , Chivu lambasted his side's lack of edge. "We were leading 2-0, 3-1 and 4-2, so this is the regret," Chivu said after the game. "We had an idea of what we should’ve done and did not do, we should’ve controlled the advantage, then when we felt them snapping at our heels, we immediately restored the two-goal cushion. "I think we failed the exam in the final minutes. It’s hard to say why we were unable to control the lead. We have to congratulate Atalanta, as they sensed that we were a bit shallow, and pumped crosses into the box, put bodies in there, while we were a little soft compared to our usual approach. sports.title: 'You don't win 345 matches just by defending' - Diego Simeone hits back at critics after breaking Luis Aragones' all-time La Liga record
sports.description: FBL-ESP-LIGA-ATLETICO-BARCELONA - AFP Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone has hit back at critics who label his side overly defensive after breaking Luis Aragones' all-time La Liga wins record on Sunday. The Argentine secured his 345th Spanish top-flight victory with a comfortable 3-0 triumph at Getafe, moving past the late club legend's long-standing benchmark of 344 wins. Argentine coach surpasses club legend Simeone claimed his 345th La Liga victory in just his 567th match , needing 189 fewer games than Aragones took to reach 344 before his final win in 2004. Goals from Alex Baena and Johnny Cardoso put Atletico in control by half-time, both assisted by Julian Alvarez . Alejandro Grimaldo added a late penalty after Djene Dakonam was sent off following a VAR review for fouling Alexander Sorloth. Simeone rejects defensive football label Reflecting on the milestone after the match, Simeone admitted the achievement meant a great deal: "It makes me happy. I don't usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this." Despite evolving Atletico's style considerably since arriving in 2011, the coach still faces familiar jibes about his tactics. Addressing the scrutiny on Spanish television channel Movistar , he added: "Then there's the constant criticism we face. I don't place much value on it, but I do take note of it. "This narrative that we're a defensive team, as if we're always playing solely to defend. You don't win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?" Longevity defines remarkable Atletico reign Taking over a struggling club almost 15 years ago, Simeone has transformed Atletico into Spanish football's established third force, disrupting Real Madrid and Barcelona while lifting eight trophies. Although rival coaches may hold higher win percentages or larger trophy hauls, few can match his resilience and consistency at the top level. Even the deepest scars of his tenure, two Champions League final defeats to Real, one on penalties and another in extra time after a stoppage-time equaliser, failed to derail him. Instead, the black-clad tactician has maintained the same touchline intensity, passing the all-time record from one Atletico great to another 22 years after Aragones set it. Atletico chase La Liga title leaders Sunday's result made it eight wins in nine league games, lifting Atletico to 31 points , just two behind Real and five adrift of leaders Barcelona. With Baena, Alvarez and Cardoso clicking, Simeone's side have built real momentum heading into the winter schedule. Sustaining this attacking sharpness will be vital if they are to turn another strong run into a genuine title charge.

technology.title: Techie turned his too-easy job interview into a trap
technology.description: Returning to work after the weekend can feel like voluntarily walking into a trap. To help readers feel a little freer, The Register therefore uses Monday mornings to serve up a new installment of " Who, Me? " It's the column in which we share your stories of mistakes, misjudgments, and occasional misanthropy. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Marshall," who told us about a job interview he endured about 20 years ago. The interview included a practical component he described as "Here's a PC, we've broken a few things in it, get it going." Marshall quickly spotted some mundane faults, such as a loose PCI card and unplugged internal cables. He felt the test was too easy. "One of the things I always checked was whether the power supply 110/230 switch was set for the UK," he told The Register . Getting the PC running earned Marshall a job offer, but he couldn't resist suggesting a tougher test. "I said to my future manager: 'Would it be a good thing to set the power supply to the wrong voltage as part of the interview test?' He said that wasn't fair." Marshall stayed in the job for two years. A couple of months after he left, his former manager sent him a short email. "Ha-ha, very funny." Marshall asked another former colleague what might have prompted that email. "It turned out somebody – I don't know if it was an interview candidate – had blown a power supply by not checking the voltage it was set to." What a coincidence! Or maybe not? "It wasn't anything to do with me," Marshall insisted. "No idea who it was." Have you held colleagues to a higher standard than the boss expected? Or left a little trap for them to trip over? In either case, click here to send email to Who, Me? We appreciate the chance to share your stories, and do so with appropriate anonymization so that contributors never step into the jaws of trouble. ®

technology.title: Google claims last week’s critical VMware bug was under attack in September
technology.description: Google’s Mandiant unit has claimed that the critical flaw VMware last week revealed in its vCenter product was under attack by a China-linked threat actor which knew of the bug in July and exploited it in September. VMware revealed several flaws on November 19. The big nasty is CVE-2026-123890, which allows unauthorized access to vCenter, the management console for hosts and guest VMs. According to seven researchers from Google’s threat intelligence group (formerly Mandiant), a crew it calls ARMORY CASTLE that it suspects of having links to the People’s Republic of China exploited CVE-2026-123890 by first compromising remote access appliances from BeyondTrust. Google’s analysis suggests the crew uses that toehold to establish access to other Linux appliances before moving deeper into victims’ networks. If the crew finds vCenter, it deploys a custom malware tool called “BONESAW” designed to slice into the VMware product. In the incident Google observed, BONESAW let attackers “forge authentication tokens, bypass MFA, and impersonate any user.” The gang put that access to work by conducting an inventory of the victim’s VMware setup, scooping up data describing the ESXi file system, attached disks, and mounted Virtual Machine File System volumes. ARMORY CASTLE also added an SSH public key to the root account’s authorized keys, and “conducted further reconnaissance and data theft on the ESXi filesystem using the root account.” Google also found evidence of BONESAW being used in July, on a server an unidentified entity had patched against CVE-2026-59309 – another authentication bypass vulnerability in vCenter. And BONESAW was just one of five tools Google thinks ARMORY CASTLE created as part of its plan to attack vCenter. It also made webshells named SLIMSAVAGE and CAGEMATCH, a backdoor called BEARBONES, and a SAML utility called SAWSNAKE. “The use of three separate specialized sets of malware and two zero-days in the course of a single campaign indicates that there are significant resources supporting ARMORY CASTLE operations,” Google’s researchers wrote. “It also shows the extent of the threat actor’s operational commitment to compromise high priority targets.” Few targets are as juicy as vCenter, because it can literally give attackers access to thousands of virtual machines and the hosts they run on. Google hasn't said how many attacks is saw on vCenter using BONESAW. The Register asked VMware if it was aware of the September attack, if it took any measures to defend its customers at the time, and to share a timeline for disclosure and remediation of CVE-2026-123890. A spokesperson responded by pointing to VMware’s Q&A document and stating “In today's threat environment, customers should assume any publicly disclosed critical vulnerability can and will be exploited by threat actors under the right conditions and should apply the recommended patches immediately.” VMware has tried to make that easier by adding non-disruptive patching to several of it

technology.title: $1 of GPT-5.1 tokens finds new ways around China’s Great Firewall
technology.description: Researchers have found new ways to evade China’s Great Firewall after spending just $1 worth of tokens. That result appeared last week in a paper titled “CircumVolve: Automated Discovery of Censorship Evasion Strategies Using Large Language Models” presented at the Conference on Computer and Communications Security run by the Association for Computing Machinery’s Special Interest Group on Security, Audit and Control. Penned by six researchers from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Colorado Boulder, and activist group the Great Firewall Report, the paper points out that finding holes in the Great Firewall is a laborious process – so just the kind of task worth handing to AI. The authors came up with a tool they call “CircumVolve” and describe as “a system for automated discovery of censorship circumvention strategies across the full network stack.” “CircumVolve combines LLM code generation with iterative feedback-driven evaluation to produce verifiable and deployable evasion techniques,” they wrote. “CircumVolve models different censorship techniques as discrete scenarios, each capturing the specific context, protocol constraints, and blocking mechanisms of real-world censors. Within each scenario, evasion strategies are represented as executable Python programs that implement packet and protocol manipulations — from rewriting TCP/IP header fields, to crafting DNS queries that exploit parser ambiguities, to modifying the internal structure of encrypted QUIC Initial packets — while maintaining protocol correctness within tolerable bounds or strategically violating it when beneficial.” The authors tested CircumVolve on simulated censorship tools used by China, Iran, Pakistan, and Kazakhstan, and on virtual private servers deployed on clouds in those countries. Those tests found the median API cost to the first successful evasion was less than $1 in token expenditure costs when using GPT-5.1. The authors acknowledge that operators of censorship infrastructure might be able to observe CircumVolve at work, but feel its relatively small payloads – 80 KB of outgoing and 150 KB of incoming traffic – and 25-45-second pauses between tests might see it fly under the radar. “CircumVolve represents a first step in leveraging LLMs to accelerate the censorship-circumvention lifecycle,” the authors wrote. “By automating the labor-intensive tasks of protocol analysis, implementation, and testing, AI-driven approaches make studying circumvention capabilities far more accessible to the comparatively under-resourced Internet freedom community [and] demonstrates how AI-assisted systems can narrow the resource gap between Internet freedom advocates and well-funded censoring states.” Lenovo finally cracks monster datacenter profits Ever since acquiring IBM’s x86 server business in 2014, Chinese hardware giant Lenovo has struggled to turn a profit from datacenter sales, even as it expanded its business into storage, networking, and selling to hypersc

NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin More than 60 years ago, scientists at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center aimed a laser skyward and fired a pulse of light at an orbiting satellite equipped with special reflectors. By measuring the time it took for the light to return, they demonstrated a new, more precise method for tracking satellites. Since then, satellite laser ranging (SLR) has grown more precise and more widely used. The technique now underpins many aspects of Earth observation, such as validating satellite orbits and mapping subtle changes to Earth’s surface. Pioneered at the Goddard Optical Research Facility—now the Goddard Geophysical and Astronomical Observatory —laser ranging is performed at more than 40 stations worldwide. In 2026, the next generation of SLR, developed by NASA scientists and tested at Goddard, began to come online. On October 12, a faster, even more precise SLR system officially debuted at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, operated by the Norwegian Mapping Authority, a NASA partner. The observatory’s remote location in the Arctic archipelago is shown in this image, acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 in July 2026. It is the first NASA next-generation SLR system in operation and the northernmost SLR facility on Earth. While the systems developed decades ago have been “workhorses” of the global laser tracking network, their age and the growing number of satellites have necessitated updates, said Stephen Merkowitz, project manager for NASA’s Space Geodesy Project . “We wanted newer systems that could track more objects, and track them more accurately and precisely,” he said. The Space Geodesy Satellite Laser Ranging system fires at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, against a backdrop of aurora borealis on October 7, 2026. NASA/Julie Horvath (KBR) Years of development, testing, and careful calibration produced the Space Geodesy Satellite Laser Ranging system now running at Ny-Ålesund. Among its features are lasers that can fire pulses thousands of times per second, up from tens of times per second, and sensors that can detect single photons, meaning that less light needs to be reflected back from a satellite. science.title: Watch live today: Amazon launching 1st batch of internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
science.description: null Another batch of Amazon internet satellites will fly on Monday morning (Nov. 23), just eight days after a launch failure doomed 40 of the spacecraft. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana on Monday, during a 29-minute window that opens at 6:09 a.m. EST (1109 GMT; 8:09 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6. Coverage will begin about 30 minutes before launch. An Ariane 6 rocket launches 32 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit from French Guiana on Feb. 12, 2026. (Image credit: ESA/CNES/Arianespace-ArianeGroup/Optique Video du CSG-P. Piron) Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. Monday's mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.

science.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
science.description: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano, former NASA astronaut Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, and NASA astronauts Frank Rubio and Bob Hines appear onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Credits: Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood Employees and guests of NASA’s Johnson Space Center celebrate the center’s 65th anniversary at the Lunar Receiving Park in Houston on Nov. 19, 2026. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration

science.description: null SpaceX set a new record with its latest satellite launch out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base 's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov. 22) at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California), on a mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) called NROL-136. It was the second launch from that pad in a little over 32 hours, after the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force . And that quick turnaround made history. Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn! 🏎️🚀🏎️🚀 November 22, 2026 "Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn!" Kiko Dontchev, SpaceX's vice president of launch, said via X on Sunday . (Pad 40 is at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.) NROL-136 was the sixth launch of 2026 so far for the NRO. All of them have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9, and all have delivered classified satellites to low Earth orbit . The launch marked another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the Space Force, and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 was the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies. With the sad passing of its star, Patrick Stewart , last month, and "Star Trek's" milestone 60th birthday taking place in 2026, this is a bittersweet salute that also holds an extra special significance. Directed by "The Next Generation's" Number One, Jonathan Frakes , in his feature film debut, " First Contact " consistently ranks as one of the finest "Star Trek" feature films among fans and critics, and those accolades are well deserved. Based on a compelling screenplay by Brannon Braga and Ronald D. Moore, "First Contact" remains as bright and beautiful as ever, brimming with bravado, heart, horror, and heroism. Not only was it a bona fide crowdpleaser when it was released by Paramount over Thanksgiving week on Nov. 22, 1996, but it was also a financial success for the studio, eventually pulling in a worldwide total of $212 million off a modest $45 million budget. science.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together.
